extracted.intended_audience: State insurance officials, Exchange administrators, QHP issuers, brokers/agents, and other stakeholders affected by Affordable Care Act Exchange and issuer standards
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the substantive compliance requirements, definitions, consumer protections, and program operations standards proposed in an HHS/CMS Notice of Proposed Rulemaking amending Parts 147, 155, and 156 (Exchange and issuer standards under the ACA). Useful for stakeholders preparing comments or planning implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity classification (NAICS/SBA thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the RFA, health insurance issuers are classified under NAICS code 524114 (Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers) with SBA size standard of $47 million average annual receipts; issuers could possibly be classified under 621491 (HMO Medical Centers) with SBA size standard $44.5 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes few comprehensive health insurance underwriters fall below these thresholds (approx. 84 of 479 issuers had ≤ $47M premium revenue in 2023). CMS seeks comment on these estimates and observes many small issuers belong to larger holding groups or have non-health lines that push revenues over thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small rural hospital definition (section 1102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of section 1102(b) of the Act, a small rural hospital is defined as a hospital located outside a metropolitan statistical area with fewer than 100 beds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS determined the proposed rule would not affect small rural hospitals, and therefore a regulatory impact analysis under section 1102(b) is not required for this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must assess anticipated costs before issuing rules whose mandates require spending in any one year above the UMRA threshold (in 2025, approximately $187 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not all costs are quantified, CMS expects combined impact on State, local, Tribal governments and private sector does not meet the UMRA definition of an unfunded mandate for this proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism consultation and consideration (E.O. 13132)
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing rules with potential Federalism implications, agencies must examine the policies' effects on State-Federal distribution of power and consult with States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS engaged in consultations (conference calls, NAIC conferences, individual State insurance official consultations) and attempted to balance State regulation interests with market stability. CMS acknowledges the proposal could limit State flexibility (e.g., changing 'lawfully present' definitions, curtailing open enrollment flexibility) but intends to preempt State law only to the extent necessary to apply these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition change: 'Lawfully present'—DACA exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual with deferred action under DHS' DACA process (8 CFR 236.22) shall not be considered 'lawfully present' as described in paragraphs (1) through (13) of the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment removes DACA recipients from being treated as lawfully present for purposes of Exchange eligibility and related programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Preponderance of the evidence'
rubrics_metrics.description: Preponderance of the evidence means proof by evidence that, compared with evidence opposing it, leads to the conclusion that the fact at issue is more likely true than not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is used elsewhere in the rule (e.g., determinations of agent/broker noncompliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent/broker noncompliance determination standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent, broker, or web-broker may be determined noncompliant if HHS finds by a preponderance of the evidence that the agent, broker, or web-broker violated applicable standards (see § 155.220(g)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule revises the introductory text to § 155.220(g)(2) to explicitly apply the preponderance standard for noncompliance findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with filing requirement for APTC eligibility ('file and reconcile')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange may not determine a tax filer eligible for APTC if HHS notifies the Exchange that APTC were made on behalf of the tax filer (or spouse) for a year and the tax filer or spouse did not comply with the requirement to file an income tax return and reconcile advance payments of the premium tax credit for that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If HHS notifies the Exchange, the Exchange must either (A) send a notification consistent with Federal Tax Information protections directly informing the filer they failed to file and reconcile and educating them to file/reconcile immediately; or (B) send a notification informing the filer or enrollee they may be at risk of being determined ineligible for APTC and educating them on the requirement without directly stating IRS indicates failure to file/reconcile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of applicant attestation for increased projected household income
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified, if an applicant attests that a tax filer's annual household income has increased or is reasonably expected to increase from available data and the Exchange has not verified MAGI-based income via paragraph (c)(2)(ii), the Exchange must accept the applicant's attestation regarding household income without further verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision applies to attestations of income increases for plan year coverage requests, reducing documentation burden where verification is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable threshold for attestation/data discrepancies (not less than 10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant's attestation of projected annual household income is materially higher than computed annual household income from specified data sources, Exchanges must use a 'reasonable threshold' established in guidance and approved by HHS, but that threshold must not be less than 10% and can include a dollar amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the attestation is above that threshold and other conditions apply (e.g., data indicates under 100% FPL while attestation is ≥100% but ≤400%), Exchanges must follow verification and procedural steps in § 155.315(f)(1)-(4). The same reasonable threshold is referenced across related verification paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification process: procedures when projected income suggests Medicaid/CHIP eligibility conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant's projected income attestation is ≥100% but ≤400% FPL and is more than the reasonable threshold above computed income that indicates projected income under 100% FPL, and the Exchange has not verified MAGI through the specified process, the Exchange must proceed in accordance with § 155.315(f)(1)-(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures applicants who might be Medicaid/CHIP-eligible are subjected to the specified verification and procedural timelines before APTC eligibility is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual eligibility redetermination: renewal and re-enrollment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the product under which an enrollee's QHP remains available through the Exchange for renewal consistent with § 147.106, the Exchange will renew the enrollee in a QHP under that product unless the enrollee terminates coverage or other specified exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no plans under that product are available, the Exchange will enroll the enrollee in a QHP under a different product offered by the same issuer to the extent permitted by State law, unless the enrollee terminates coverage. Paragraph (n) adds additional consumer protections for redeterminations (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional consumer protection for annual redeterminations: $5 premium remaining rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If an enrollee does not submit an updated eligibility application by the last day to make plan selections for Jan 1 effective coverage and the enrollee's portion of the premium after APTC through the redetermination process would be $0, the Exchange must decrease the amount of the advance payment applied so that the remaining monthly premium owed equals $5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federally facilitated Exchanges and SBEs on the Federal platform must apply this for benefit years on/after 2026; State-based Exchanges must adhere for benefit years on/after 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium payment threshold policy (percentage-based, uniform application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges may, and Federally facilitated Exchanges and SBEs on the Federal platform will, allow issuers to implement a percentage-based premium payment threshold policy based on net premium after APTC, provided the threshold policy is applied uniformly to all applicants and enrollees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits issuers to set payment thresholds (e.g., required proportion of premium paid) but requires uniform application across enrollees/applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open enrollment period dates (for benefit years ≥ 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: For benefit years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, the annual open enrollment period begins on November 1 and extends through December 15 of the calendar year preceding the benefit year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For those benefit years coverage must be effective January 1 for QHP selections received on or before December 15. This curtails previous State flexibility in setting later OEP end dates but is intended to limit overall costs and burdens while allowing certain SEP administration flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special enrollment period metal-level change allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning January 2022, if an enrollee or dependents become newly ineligible for cost-sharing reductions (CSRs) and are enrolled in a silver-level QHP, the Exchange must allow the enrollee and dependents to change to a QHP one metal level higher or lower if they elect to change. No later than January 1, 2024, if newly ineligible for APTC, the Exchange must allow change to a QHP of any metal level if they elect to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions expand consumer choice when subsidy or CSR eligibility changes occur, with phased timing for APTC-related changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special enrollment period (SEP) pre-enrollment verification requirement (75% verification standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Exchange must conduct pre-enrollment verification of applicants' eligibility for special enrollment periods and meets this requirement if it verifies eligibility for a number of individuals newly enrolling through SEPs that equals at least 75 percent of all special enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Exchange is unable to verify eligibility for individuals for whom verification is required, those individuals are not eligible for enrollment through the Exchange. Individuals retain the right to appeal under § 155.505(b)(1)(iii). Requests for modification may be granted under § 155.315(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guaranteed availability cross-references in § 147.104
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 147.104(b)(2)(i) is revised to reference § 155.420(d)(12) (plan and benefit display errors) and § 155.420(d)(13) (eligibility for insurance affordability programs or enrollment in the Exchange).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cross-references link guaranteed availability protections to specific special enrollment period/plan display error provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Health Benefits (EHB) exclusions by plan year (§ 156.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: For plan years beginning before Jan 1, 2026, issuers may not include routine non‑pediatric dental services, routine non‑pediatric eye exams, long‑term/custodial nursing home care benefits, or non‑medically necessary orthodontia as EHB. For plan years beginning any day in 2026, issuers may not include those items or sex‑trait modification as EHB. For plan years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2027, issuers may not include routine non‑pediatric eye exams, long‑term/custodial nursing home care, non‑medically necessary orthodontia, or sex‑trait modification as EHB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This phases the exclusion of certain services from EHB and adds 'sex‑trait modification' to exclusions beginning in 2026/2027 per timeline above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Actuarial Value (AV) de minimis variation (§ 156.140)
rubrics_metrics.description: The allowable variation in AV of a health plan that does not result in a material difference in the true dollar value of the plan is −4 percentage points and +2 percentage points, except for expanded bronze plans (as defined) where allowable variation is −4 and +5 percentage points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded bronze plans are bronze plans that cover and pay for at least one major service before the deductible or meet HDHP requirements under section 223(c)(2) of the IRC; reserved paragraph (2) remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP issuer participation requirement: compliance with benefit design standards (§ 156.200)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each QHP issuer must ensure that each QHP complies with benefit design standards as defined in § 156.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a direct issuer obligation to meet the statutory/regulatory benefit design requirements when offering QHPs through Exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis AV variation for silver plan variation (§ 156.400)
rubrics_metrics.description: De minimis variation for a silver plan variation means a −1-percentage point and +1-percentage point allowable AV variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the narrower allowable AV variation for silver plan variations.
